text: Note: censoring() function applicable continuous VPC. censor observed data lower limit quantification (LLOQ), include censoring() function simulated() use lloq argument specify either variable data specific value censoring. blq argument creates logical TRUE/FALSE data indicates whether value limit quantification typically defined rows DV < LLOQ data. Using censoring() function censor observed data lower limit quantification plotting, simulated data still plotted. Censoring using numeric value.  tidyvpc package also allows use LLOQ values within data different LLOQ level stratification variable. ’ll set LLOQ value 50 Study 25 Study B calculate statistics 10%, 50%, 90% quantiles.  tidyvpc package also supports usage censoring() ALQ data, similar usage BLQ data. plot vpc include percentage ALQ plot, ’d run plot(vpc, censoring.type = "alq"). using censoring() ALQ BLQ data, set censoring.type = "" plot() function display percentage BLQ ALQ plots grid resulting VPC plot.  want return percentage BLQ /ALQ plots individually elements list, instead arranged grid, use censoring.output argument e.g., plot_list <- plot(vpc, censoring.type = "", censoring.output = "list").
code: vpc <- observed(obs_data, x=TIME, y=DV) %>%     simulated(sim_data, y=DV) %>%     censoring(blq=(DV < 25), lloq=25) %>%     binning(bin = "jenks", nbins = 5) %>%     vpcstats()  plot(vpc, censoring.type = "blq") obs_data$LLOQ <- obs_data[, ifelse(STUDY == "Study A", 50, 25)]  vpc <- observed(obs_data, x=TIME, y=DV) %>%     simulated(sim_data, y=DV) %>%     censoring(blq=(DV < LLOQ), lloq=LLOQ) %>%     stratify(~ STUDY) %>%     binning(bin = "pam", nbins = 4) %>%     vpcstats(qpred = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))  plot(vpc, censoring.type = "blq", facet.scales = "fixed") obs_data$ULOQ <- obs_data[, ifelse(STUDY == "Study A", 125, 100)]  vpc <- observed(obs_data, x = TIME, y = DV) |>   simulated(sim_data, y = DV) |>   censoring(alq = DV > ULOQ, uloq = ULOQ) |>   stratify(~ STUDY) |>   binning(bin = NTIME) |>   vpcstats(qpred = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9)) obs_data$LLOQ <- obs_data[, ifelse(STUDY == "Study A", 50, 25)] obs_data$ULOQ <- obs_data[, ifelse(STUDY == "Study A", 125, 100)]  vpc <- observed(obs_data, x = TIME, y = DV) |>   simulated(sim_data, y = DV) |>   censoring(blq = DV < LLOQ, lloq = LLOQ,  alq = DV > ULOQ, uloq = ULOQ) |>   stratify(~ STUDY) |>   binning(bin = NTIME) |>   vpcstats(qpred = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))  plot(vpc, censoring.type = "both", facet.scales = "fixed")

title: Introduction to continuous VPC
text: Note: predcorrect() function applicable continuous VPC. derive prediction corrected VPC (pcVPC), use predcorrect() function. predcorrect() function requires argument, pred, unquoted variable name population prediction variable data. predcorrect() function may called either specifying binning()/binless(). using binless() function predcorrect(), LOESS pcVPC performed. Note: model fit using log scale DV, make sure include argument log = TRUE predcorrect() perform appropriate prediction correction calculation. Prediction corrected using binning methods.  LOESS prediction corrected using binless method 10%, 50%, 90% quantiles. optimize = TRUE, LOESS smoothing parameter, span, automatically optimized using AIC.  specify smoothing value LOESS pcVPC instead optimizing AIC, use span argument binless() function. span argument numeric value [0,1], higher values providing smoother fit. Remember, also include smoothing parameters AQR using lambda argument set optimize = FALSE.
code: vpc <- observed(obs_data, x=TIME, y=DV) %>%     simulated(sim_data, y=DV) %>%     stratify(~GENDER) %>%     binning(bin = NTIME) %>%     predcorrect(pred=PRED) %>%     vpcstats()  plot(vpc) vpc <- observed(obs_data, x=TIME, y=DV) %>%     simulated(sim_data, y=DV) %>%     stratify(~GENDER) %>%     binless(qpred = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), optimize = TRUE) %>%     predcorrect(pred=PRED) %>%     vpcstats()  plot(vpc) vpc <- observed(obs_data, x=TIME, y=DV) %>%     simulated(sim_data, y=DV) %>%     predcorrect(pred=PRED) %>%     binless(optimize = FALSE, lambda = c(.95,3,1.2), span = .6) %>%     vpcstats()  plot(vpc)

title: Quantitative Predictive Check (QPC) scoring for VPC
text: Visual Predictive Check (VPC) typically assessed visually checking: calibration (observations inside simulated prediction intervals?) bias trend (model systematically miss certain x regions?) sharpness (prediction intervals unnecessarily wide?) Quantitative Predictive Check (QPC) score tidyvpc numeric summary features, computed existing tidyvpcobj vpcstats(). QPC produces table qpc.stats composite scalar qpc_score (lower better) can used automated model comparison optimization.

title: Quantitative Predictive Check (QPC) scoring for VPC
text: QPC computed o$stats (data.table produced vpcstats()), contains (continuous VPCs) curve points across quantiles: qname: quantile curve (e.g. q0.05, q0.5, q0.95) y: observed curve value x md: simulated median curve x lo, hi: simulated confidence interval bounds x quantile curve curve point, QPC derives: Coverage: whether y∈[lo,hi]y \[lo, hi] Deviation: |y−md||y - md| relative PI half-width Drift: Spearman correlation residuals (y−md)(y-md) versus x (monotonic bias) Sharpness: interval width (penalizes “variance inflation”) Proper interval score (Winkler): rewards narrow intervals penalizes misses aggregated across curves combined qpc_score user-controlled weights.

title: Quantitative Predictive Check (QPC) scoring for VPC
text: qpcstats() prints scalar qpc_score plus component breakdown. component designed 0 = best larger values = worse. high level: Coverage penalties measure calibration (observed curves inside simulated uncertainty bands?). MAE drift penalties measure agreement bias structure (far whether residuals trend x). Sharpness interval penalties discourage “variance inflation” (overly wide bands can artificially increase coverage). concretely (continuous VPC): Median coverage penalty (coverage_penalty_med): computed median quantile curve (curve closest q=0.5q=0.5): 1−mean(𝟏[y∈[lo,hi]]) 1 - \text{mean}(\mathbf{1}[y \[lo,hi]])  Lower better; 0 means observed median curve always inside simulated band. Tail coverage penalty (coverage_penalty_tails): computed lowest highest quantile curves available (typically q=0.05q=0.05 q=0.95q=0.95), averaged: (1−coveragelow)+(1−coveragehigh)2 \frac{(1-\text{coverage}_{low}) + (1-\text{coverage}_{high})}{2} MAE penalty (mae_penalty_all): based deviation scaled PI half-width: dev_mid=|y−md|(hi−lo)/2 dev\_mid = \frac{|y-md|}{(hi-lo)/2}  bounded [0,1][0,1] averaged across curves. highlights “large misses relative model’s uncertainty”. Drift penalty (rho_penalty_all): absolute Spearman correlation residuals (y−md)(y-md) vs x (averaged across curves), bounded [0,1][0,1]. Values near 0 indicate monotonic bias trend across x; larger values indicate systematic drift. Sharpness penalty (sharpness_penalty): penalizes wide bands using relative width: width_rel=(hi−lo)|md| width\_{rel} = \frac{(hi-lo)}{|md|}  default (single-VPC scoring), mapped [0,1)[0,1) bounded transform: 1−e−max⁡(width_rel,0) 1 - e^{-\max(width\_{rel}, 0)}  Optionally, can anchor sharp_ref cross-model comparability. Interval penalty (interval_penalty): based Winkler interval score nominal PI level (1−α)(1-\alpha): $$ = (hi-lo) + \\frac{2}{\\alpha}(lo-y)\\mathbf{1}[y<lo] + \\frac{2}{\\alpha}(y-hi)\\mathbf{1}[y>hi] $$ rewards narrow intervals strongly penalizes misses. default apply bounded transform normalized score; optionally can anchor interval_ref. Finally: qpc_score=∑iwi⋅penaltyi qpc\_score = \sum_i w_i \cdot penalty_i w named weight vector (med_cov, tail_cov, mae, drift, sharp, interval).

title: Quantitative Predictive Check (QPC) scoring for VPC
text: One failure mode purely visual scoring wide simulated confidence intervals can appear “cover everything”. QPC penalizes via sharpness interval score components. artificially add noise simulated DV values create wider confidence intervals, compare qpc.stats. QPC summary: baseline vs noisy simulations (0 = best; lower qpc_score better) comparison typically see: sharpness_penalty increases wider prediction intervals interval_penalty increases Winkler score increases width (even coverage improves) therefore qpc_score tends increase (worse) Compare two plots:
